summary: At just 1.3 square miles, Dos Palos packs roughly 5,700 people into a footprint smaller than many regional shopping centers, yet step outside the compact grid and you're staring across the vast, flat agricultural expanse of the San Joaquin Valley — cotton, almonds, and dairy operations stretching toward the Coast Ranges to the west, which catch the last light on summer evenings. This is unmistakably a farming town: agriculture and its supporting industries (processing, equipment, logistics) anchor the local economy, and the median household income of about $50,500 paired with a median home price near $285,300 yields a price-to-income ratio around 5.6× — far more approachable than coastal California, though still a stretch without dual incomes. Commuting is part of the bargain; Los Banos sits roughly 20 miles north on Highway 152, and Fresno is over an hour east, so many residents drive significant distances for work beyond ag-sector jobs. With 9.7 hours of daily sunshine on average and annual highs around 79°F, summers are genuinely hot and dry in the Central Valley tradition, while winters are mild but foggy — tule fog can blanket the valley floor for days. The town has a small commercial corridor with basic retail and fast-food options, but grocery variety and sit-down dining are limited enough that a trip to a larger city is routine. Dos Palos is a place where the housing math works better than most of California, but the tradeoff is distance from almost everything that isn't farmland.
